title: Efficient purification and concentration of viruses from a large body of high turbidity seawater
author: Sun, Xiao, et al.

steps.title: Collect seawater sample
steps.instruction: Collect more than 300 L of subsurface seawater at 2 m depth from Yangshan Deep‑Water Port, noting a suspended matter content of approximately 3.4 g L⁻¹ (wet weight). Keep the samples on ice and transport to the laboratory as quickly as possible.

steps.title: Fix aliquot for enumeration
steps.instruction: In the field, add 0.02 µm‑filtered formalin (37–40 % w/v formaldehyde, Sangon) to 500 mL of the collected water to reach a final formaldehyde concentration of 2 % v/v. Mix gently.

steps.title: Prefilter seawater
steps.instruction: Gravity‑filter the remaining seawater (up to 150 L for the optimized workflow) sequentially through eight layers of gauze and nylon fiber filters of 100 µm, 50 µm, 25 µm and 10 µm pore size. Store the filtrate in sterile containers at 4 °C until further processing. Retain the settled matter for later virus extraction.

steps.title: Concentrate viruses by TFF
steps.instruction: Process the prefiltered filtrate using a tangential flow filtration (TFF) system until the retentate volume reaches approximately 1 L (viral concentrate I). This step takes less than 20 h and yields a virus concentration of about 3.11 × 10⁸ VLP mL⁻¹. Collect the TFF permeate for the membrane‑rinse step.

steps.title: Rinse TFF membrane
steps.instruction: Wash the TFF membrane with 20 L of the previously collected TFF permeate. Collect the wash eluate (≈1 L), which contains about 5.98 × 10⁷ VLP mL⁻¹, and add this eluate to the viral concentrate obtained in the previous step.

steps.title: Extract viruses from settled matter
steps.instruction: Separate the settled matter (≈509.8 g) from the original 150 L seawater. Process this material (method not detailed) to obtain a viral concentrate of 500 mL containing roughly 7.51 × 10⁸ VLP g⁻¹, corresponding to a total of about 3.83 × 10¹¹ VLPs.

steps.title: Combine viral fractions
steps.instruction: Pool the three viral fractions: 1 L from the TFF water fraction, 1 L from the membrane rinse, and 0.5 L from the settled‑matter extraction, resulting in a combined volume of 2.5 L.

steps.title: Reconcentrate with centrifugal filter
steps.instruction: Load the 2.5 L combined viral solution onto a Centricon Plus‑70 centrifugal filter device. Centrifuge according to the manufacturer’s protocol until the final retentate volume is approximately 4.28 mL. The final concentrate contains about 1.63 × 10¹¹ VLP mL⁻¹ (16.30 × 10¹⁰ VLP mL⁻¹).

steps.title: Wash final concentrate
steps.instruction: Perform a wash step on the Centricon device with sterile buffer (volume not specified) and repeat centrifugation to remove residual salt ions from the viral concentrate.

steps.title: Calculate recovery and concentration factors
steps.instruction: Determine viral recovery efficiency as (final VLP count ÷ original VLP count) × 100 % = 67.10 %. Compute the volume concentration factor (150 L ÷ 4.28 mL ≈ 3.5 × 10⁴) and the viral‑density concentration factor (1.63 × 10¹¹ VLP mL⁻¹ ÷ 6.95 × 10⁶ VLP mL⁻¹ ≈ 2.3 × 10⁴).
